title: The Old Way vs. The Quantum Way
style_suffix: Cinematic TV commercial, photorealistic, natural lip sync, 35mm lens, shallow depth of field, punchy contrast grade, subtle film grain. No text, no letters, no logos, no signs anywhere; any screens show only soft abstract shapes. Sound: clear natural dialogue and light room ambience.

shots.prompt: Photorealistic portrait of a cheerful, slightly smug middle-aged man called Busywork: rumpled beige cardigan over a mustard shirt, crooked brown tie, messy thinning hair, round tortoiseshell glasses, a lanyard with a blank white badge, holding a tall wobbling stack of paper files against his chest and grinning mischievously at the camera. Standing in a dim, cluttered corporate office. Cinematic lighting, 35mm, shallow depth of field. No text, no letters, no logos.

The woman from the reference image, same face, hair and grey blazer, now sits in a bright open-plan sales office cubicle in daytime, a small white wireless earbud in each ear. She laughs warmly and says clearly in a confident American female voice: "Perfect. Tuesday at ten. See you then!" She taps her laptop once and instantly smiles at the next person: "Hi Mark, it's Maya." Energetic, upbeat, slight handheld camera.

The man from the reference image, same face, messy hair, rumpled white shirt and loose tie, slowly rises and peeks over a grey office cubicle wall, bewildered and exasperated, and says in a frustrated American male voice: "How have you talked to eleven people in sixty-six minutes? I can't get anyone on the phone!" Camera from the neighbouring cubicle looking up at him, comedic timing.

The woman from the reference image, same face, hair and grey blazer, sitting in a bright open-plan office cubicle in daytime, pulls one small white earbud out of her ear, swivels her chair toward someone standing above her and says with a friendly, amused grin in a confident American female voice: "You haven't heard of Connect and Sell? A week of prospecting in four hours." She pops the earbud back in and turns back to her laptop.

The grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image perches casually on the edge of a cluttered office desk. At the desk sits the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image, on a desk phone. The cardigan man looks straight into the camera and says cheerfully in a smug, playful older American male voice: "I'm Busywork. I live in every sales team." Then he tips a huge stack of business cards onto the tired man's lap; cards scatter everywhere and the tired man groans. Comedic, punchy, slight push-in.

In a grey office cubicle, the grinning older man in the beige cardigan and round glasses from the first reference image slaps a thick printed phone list down onto the desk in front of the frustrated man in the white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image and says cheerfully: "Keep dialing, champ." The frustrated man stares at the pile in despair. Comedic timing, loud paper thud.

Over-the-shoulder shot from just behind and to the right of the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image, sitting at a bright modern office desk in daytime with a small white earbud in her ear, looking at an open laptop that fills the right half of the frame. The laptop screen is a flat, evenly lit, solid bright chroma-key green filling the entire display, with nothing on it. Camera locked off on a tripod, completely static. She speaks cheerfully: "Tuesday at ten works. See you then!" and taps the trackpad.

Late afternoon in a cluttered office. the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image squints at his monitor, surrounded by printouts and sticky notes, rubbing his temples, and mutters wearily: "Three hours on one account, and I still don't know who signs." Then the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image drops a thick pile of printouts onto his lap with a thud and says brightly: "Only three more hours, champ." The monitor faces away from camera.

Over-the-shoulder shot from just behind and to the right of the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image, at a bright modern office desk, looking at an open laptop that fills the right half of the frame. The laptop screen is a flat, evenly lit, solid bright chroma-key green filling the entire display, with nothing on it. Camera locked off on a tripod, completely static. She clicks once, leans back with a satisfied smile, glances back over her shoulder at the camera and says: "Done. Three seconds."

In a small client conference room, the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image scribbles frantically on a yellow legal pad, head down, while a woman across the table keeps talking. His pen runs out; he shakes it in frustration, sighs and says under his breath: "Hang on, can you repeat that?" Comedic, natural light.

In a bright client conference room, the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image sits across the table from a friendly female office manager in a navy cardigan. Maya places her phone face-down on the table and says warmly: "Mind if I turn on my notetaker, so I can give you my full attention?" The office manager smiles and says: "Please." Maya leans in, fully engaged, eye contact.

Inside a car in a sunny office parking lot. the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image gets into the driver's seat and tosses a business card onto a messy pile of dozens of business cards on the passenger seat, saying: "I'll enter that later." Then the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image is revealed sitting in the passenger seat, seatbelt on, grinning at the camera, and says: "He won't."

the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image walks confidently out of a glass office building to her car in a sunny parking lot, holding her phone up and speaking into it: "Claude, log my meeting with Dana, send her the recap, and set a follow-up for Tuesday." She smiles as her phone chimes, and gets into her car. Tracking shot.

the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image sits at his office desk beside a monitor that faces away from camera, next to a filing cabinet with its drawers hanging open and paper contracts spilling out. He turns to the camera with regret and says: "I wish I'd done a better job tracking contract end dates."

the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image sits relaxed in a bright modern office, turns to the camera with a confident smile and says: "I ran every past engagement through Quantum's AI Lead Finder. Twenty-five hundred competitive contracts, coming up."

Night, an empty dark office lit only by a desk lamp. the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image holds a cell phone to his ear, exhausted, and says softly: "Hey hon... it's going to be another late night." Behind him, the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image cheerfully tips a huge box of envelopes and paper mail over his head; it rains down onto his lap and desk. Comedic.

A fit, happy man in his fifties, a business owner, jogging on a scenic riverside trail at golden hour, wearing running gear and a small wireless earbud. He answers a call without stopping, smiling, and says in a relaxed, confident American male voice: "No problem. I'll get my team on it right away." He keeps running, enjoying the sunset. Tracking shot.

In a bright modern office, the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image peers over the shoulder of the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the second reference image, who is calmly finishing her work and closing her laptop. He looks at the camera, shrugs sadly and says: "Well... nobody needs me anymore." He slowly shuffles out of frame.

the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image closes her laptop at a bright desk at the end of the day, picks up her bag, turns to the camera and says with a confident smile: "Same job. Same hours. Different system." Warm golden light.

Camera inside a car, filming from the passenger seat toward the driver. The tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image drops into the driver's seat after a sales call, sighs, and flicks a business card onto a messy pile of dozens of business cards on the passenger seat in the foreground, saying: "I'll enter that later." Sunny office parking lot outside the windows.

Inside a car, the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the reference image sits in the passenger seat on top of a pile of business cards, seatbelt on. He turns slowly to the camera with a smug grin and says: "He won't." Sunny parking lot outside. Comedic beat.

the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image perches casually on the edge of a cluttered office desk where the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image sits on a desk phone. The cardigan man looks straight into the camera and says in a smug, playful older American male voice: "I'm Manny. Manny Manual. I live in every sales team." Then he tips a huge stack of business cards onto the tired man's lap; cards scatter everywhere and the tired man groans. Comedic, punchy, slight push-in.

the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image sits at a bright modern desk. Without looking away from her work she asks: "Who signs at Riverside?" One of her team members in matching charcoal polo shirts with a thin lime-green collar stripe, a sharp young man standing right beside her desk holding a tablet, answers instantly: "Doctor Reyes. Dana recommends." She smiles: "Perfect." Crisp, fast, witty.

the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image sits at a bright modern desk. Beside her desk a small sleek white conveyor belt glides past, delivering neat folders one after another with a soft whir. She glances over, picks up the next folder without breaking stride, and says with a grin: "Next." Playful, slightly surreal, no text on the folders.

Close-up at a bright modern desk: the hand of the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image taps a large round glowing lime-green button on the desk; it lights up with a satisfying chime. She says, relaxed and pleased: "Done." The button has no text or symbols on it.

Early evening in a bright modern office. the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image sits at her desk while behind her four team members in matching charcoal polo shirts with a thin lime-green collar stripe work calmly and efficiently at screens facing away from camera. A friendly coworker in a denim jacket leans in and asks: "Want to grab dinner?" Maya glances back at her busy team, smiles, and says: "Yeah... I think they've got it from here." She grabs her bag and stands up.

Saturday morning in a sunny family kitchen. the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image, now in a wrinkled polo shirt, hunches over a laptop and piles of paperwork at the kitchen table. His wife, in a team sports hoodie and holding car keys, stands in the doorway with two kids in soccer uniforms behind her and says: "Honey, it's Saturday. The kids have a game today." He looks up guiltily: "I know, I know. I'm coming."

In the same sunny family kitchen, the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image stands up from the table to leave. the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image suddenly appears beside him, grabs his arm firmly and says with a wicked grin: "Not so fast. You're with me today." Then he throws his head back and lets out a big theatrical villain laugh. Comedic.

A cluttered office. the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image clings to the arm of the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image. The tired man finally pulls his arm free, stands tall and says firmly: "I can't do this anymore." The cardigan man, wounded and pleading, clutches his chest and says: "But... it's always been us." Comedic breakup-scene drama, soap-opera lighting.

A bright modern open-plan office. the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image walks up to the desk of the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the first reference image, a little sheepish. She smiles warmly. One of her team members in matching charcoal polo shirts with a thin lime-green collar stripe rolls a chair over for him; he sits down, relieved, and she says: "Welcome to the team." He exhales and laughs. Uplifting, warm light.

Night. the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the reference image sits alone in a dark, empty office on an overturned box of paper files, under one flickering fluorescent light. He looks around the empty room and calls out hopefully: "Anybody? ... Anybody need a spreadsheet?" Silence. A single sheet of paper drifts to the floor. Comedic, melancholy.

the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image perches casually on the edge of a cluttered office desk where the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image sits on a desk phone. The cardigan man looks straight into the camera and says in a smug, playful older American male voice: "I'm Bob. Bogged Down Bob. I live in every sales team." Then he tips a huge stack of business cards onto the tired man's lap; cards scatter everywhere and the tired man groans. Comedic, punchy, slight push-in.

the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image perches casually on the edge of a cluttered office desk where the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image sits on a desk phone. The cardigan man looks straight into the camera and says in a smug, playful older American male voice: "I'm Bob. Bog Down Bob. I live in every sales team." Then he tips a huge stack of business cards onto the tired man's lap; cards scatter everywhere and the tired man groans. Comedic, punchy, slight push-in.

A long office corridor. the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image strides toward the exit with his jacket over his shoulder, determined, dragging the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image along the floor, who is lying on his stomach clinging desperately to his leg with both arms. The cardigan man wails: "Wait! Don't go! We had something!" The tired man keeps walking without looking down. Slapstick comedy, tracking shot.

A sunny youth soccer field on a Saturday. the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image, now relaxed in a casual polo and sunglasses on his head, arrives on the sideline next to his wife, who wears a team hoodie. She looks around behind him and asks, teasing: "Honey... where's Bog Down Bob?" He smiles, genuinely relaxed, and says: "I don't think we'll be seeing much of him anymore." Warm golden light, families cheering in the background.

A sunny youth soccer field. A joyful seven-year-old in a soccer uniform sprints across the grass toward the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image, in a casual polo, shouting: "Daddy! You finally made it!" and leaps into his arms for a big hug. He laughs and spins the kid around. Heartwarming, golden hour, slow-motion ending.

Inside an American left-hand-drive sedan in a sunny office parking lot. Camera sits in the front passenger seat looking left toward the driver's seat. The tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image drops into the DRIVER'S seat on the left, directly behind the steering wheel, sighs, and flicks a business card onto a messy pile of dozens of business cards on the passenger seat in the foreground, saying: "I'll enter that later." The steering wheel is in front of him, on the left side of the car.

Inside an American left-hand-drive sedan in a sunny parking lot. Camera is in the driver's seat looking right. The grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the reference image sits in the FRONT PASSENGER seat on the right side of the car, the glovebox and dashboard in front of him, the passenger door and window behind him, seatbelt on, sitting on top of a pile of business cards. He turns slowly to the camera with a smug grin and says: "He won't." Comedic beat.

Camera in the back seat of an American sedan, centered, looking forward through the windshield at a sunny office parking lot. On the LEFT side of the frame, the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image sits in the driver's seat directly behind the steering wheel. On the RIGHT side of the frame the front passenger seat is buried under a messy pile of dozens of business cards. He sighs, turns his head and flicks one more business card onto the pile, saying: "I'll enter that later."

Camera in the back seat of an American sedan, centered, looking forward. On the LEFT the tired man in the white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image sits behind the steering wheel. On the RIGHT, in the front passenger seat on top of a pile of business cards, the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image slowly turns around to face the camera with a smug grin and says: "He won't." Comedic beat.

Exterior, a sunny office parking lot. The tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image stands at the open door of his sedan, leans in and flicks a business card onto a messy pile of dozens of business cards spilling across the car seat, sighs and says: "I'll enter that later." Then he slumps down into the car. Camera outside the car at waist height, side view, no steering wheel visible.

the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image perches casually on the edge of a cluttered office desk where the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image sits on a desk phone. The cardigan man looks straight into the camera and says in a smug, playful older American male voice: "I'm Bob. Bog Down Bob. I live in every sales team." Then he tips a huge stack of business cards onto the tired man's lap; cards scatter everywhere and the tired man drops his head into his hands. Only the cardigan man speaks. Comedic, punchy, slight push-in.

In a grey office cubicle, the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the first reference image slaps a thick printed phone list down onto the desk in front of the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the second reference image and says cheerfully and clearly: "Keep dialing, buddy." The tired man stares at the pile in despair. Only the cardigan man speaks.

In a small client conference room, a friendly female office manager in a navy cardigan says clearly: "We have three locations, and the copiers keep going down." Across the table the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image scribbles frantically on a yellow legal pad, head down. His pen runs out; he shakes it and says: "Sorry, can you repeat that?" Comedic, natural light.

In a bright client conference room, the woman in the grey blazer with her hair pulled back from the reference image sits across the table from a friendly female office manager in a navy cardigan. Maya places her phone face-down on the table and says warmly and clearly: "Mind if I let AI take the notes, so I can give you my full attention?" The office manager smiles and says: "Please." Maya leans in, fully engaged, eye contact.

Night. the grinning older man in the beige cardigan, mustard shirt, round glasses and lanyard from the reference image sits alone in a dark, empty office on an overturned box of paper files, under one flickering fluorescent light. He looks around the empty room and calls out hopefully: "Anybody? ... Anybody need some data entry?" Nobody answers. A single sheet of paper drifts to the floor. Comedic, melancholy.

A sunny youth soccer field. A joyful seven-year-old boy in a soccer uniform sprints across the grass toward the tired man in the rumpled white shirt and loose tie from the reference image and shouts loudly and clearly in a child's voice: "Daddy! You made it!" He leaps into his dad's arms for a big hug; the dad laughs and spins him around. Heartwarming, golden hour.

The woman from the reference image, same face, now in running gear with her hair in a ponytail and a small wireless earbud, jogging on a scenic riverside trail at golden hour. She answers a call without stopping, smiling, and says in a relaxed, confident American female voice: "No problem. I'll get my team on it right away." She keeps running, enjoying the sunset. Tracking shot.
